sentences.text: This reptile possessed a relatively flat, heavily armored body that strongly resembled a turtle.
Its skull was very robust and broad at the back, narrowing toward the front snout.
The animal had exceptionally strong jaws that likely supported powerful musculature.
Round-shaped teeth lined both the palate and jaws, including huge molars designed for crushing.
Macroplacus measured approximately one meter in total length.
Fossil remains have been discovered in Germany at a site near Hinterstein.
It led an amphibious lifestyle but remained poorly adapted to fully marine environments.
The creature swam slowly through shallow coastal waters to hunt primarily for shellfish.
Large, hemispheric teeth on the roof of the mouth helped break open mollusk shells.
The classification of Macroplacus is controversial, though it is usually placed in the Cyamodontidae or Placochelyidae.
It is a placodont reptile that looks similar to turtles but is probably related to diapsids.
This species lived during the Rhaetian age of the upper Triassic, between 205.6 and 201.6 million years ago.
